chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Saif ibn Umayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sick person in the month of Ramadan who does not recover until he dies; he said: His fasts are not made up for him. And about the menstruating woman who dies in the month of Ramadan; he said: Her fasts are not made up for her.
ai.seo_question: Do missed fasts need to be made up for a person who dies in Ramadan due to illness or menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that missed fasts are not obligatory for a sick person or menstruating woman who die in Ramadan, as their incapacity was permanent rather than temporary. This ruling distinguishes their status from those who die with the specific intention or ability to complete the fasts later, reflecting the Shia principle that qada is tied to the capacity to fulfill the obligation. The narration underscores the mercy in Islamic jurisprudence by relieving the deceased's estate of this specific debt when the impediment persisted until death.
